cards.title: Two verbs, two jobs
cards.body: **be** says who or how you are. **have** says what is yours.
points: be: name, job, place, feeling, age → **I am a student. She is tired.**
have: things, family, pets → **I have a brother. He has a car.**

cards.title: Form
cards.body: Three forms for *be*, two for *have*. The subject picks the form.
points: **I am tired. She is tired. They are tired.**
**I have a car. She has a car. They have a car.**

cards.title: be, not have
cards.body: Czech says *mám* for age, hunger, thirst and fear (*mám 30 let · mám hlad*). English says **be** + adjective.
points: Hunger, thirst: **I am hungry. I am thirsty.**
Fear, cold, heat: **I am afraid. I am cold. I am hot.**

cards.title: Common mistakes
cards.body: The form is easy. The mistake is choosing *have* where English wants *be*.
points: *He have a car* → **He has a car**
